memory_update.text: CEG, TLN, and VST are the clearest direct nuclear/firm-power asset-owner candidates because they have named hyperscaler PPAs with MW scale and contract duration evidence.
ETR is a high-priority regulated-utility candidate because Meta-linked generation and transmission approvals create a concrete rate-base/capex recovery research path rather than generic AI exposure.
GEV should be tracked as a power-equipment chokepoint candidate because it has direct AI data-center turbine orders and broader grid/substation/electrification exposure.
Further Layer 1B passes should separately test NEE, D, SO, BE, PWR, ETN, CEG peers, uranium/fuel-chain names, battery integrators, and transmission contractors against contract-level evidence.

For this node, signed PPAs, public-service-commission approvals, interconnection/transmission milestones, turbine delivery schedules, and capex recovery mechanisms are stronger evidence than broad statements about AI electricity demand.
